Hi Jane / Acme team,

Thanks for the call this morning. Per our discussion, attached is a cleanredline (Acme_OrderForm_Redline_v3.docx) with two focused asks so we can finalize the order form without reopening the whole billing model: 

1) Clarify the "floor trigger" behavior when monthly consumption falls below the committed band mid-quarter. Our redline replaces the automatic immediate floor charge with a 45-day "fallout window" and an ability for Acme to make up shortfall within the window before fees apply.

2) Add a short-term stabilizer credit (one-time, applied in first invoice) to smooth the onboarding delta that you highlighted. We propose a $25K credit to offset anticipated initial usage variance.

Quick asks: can you confirm whether the fallout window is acceptable, and whether procurement/legal will accept language that ties the floor to an "actualized trailing 30-day average" rather than single-day snapshots?

If that direction works, I'll loop in Laura to propose precise legal wording and get this ready for signature. If you prefer an alternate numeric window or a hard immediate floor, we can iterate but it'll likely require a pricing concession on our side.

Attachments: Acme_OrderForm_Redline_v3.docx (redline), RBI_suggested_language_floor_stabilizer.txt (proposed clause)

Thanks,

Dylan —

Thanks for the doc. High level feedback from Acme legal/procurement: we like the concept of a fallout window but need clarity on two points before sign-off: 

- Measurement: we cannot agree to a trailing 30-day average to avoid single-day spikes — we prefer a 60-day trailing average to reduce volatility.
- Remedy: the fallout window cannot be solely a make-up obligation (Acme may not be able to ramp usage that fast). We will accept a make-up provision only if there is a clearly defined cap on retroactive billing (e.g., no more than 25% of the missing usage billed retroactively) and a one-time hard cap on total retro charges.

Separately, procurement is asking whether the stabilizer credit can be structured as a conditional credit (applied only if year-one net churn < 8%). If year-one churn exceeds that, the credit would recoup as a one-time invoice in Q4. That condition is acceptable to us but we'd like Redwood's confirmation that the measurement definition of churn will be the number of active integration seats (or equivalent) and not token-based usage.

We also redlined a proposed alternative clause and embedded comments in your doc — see attached (I forwarded it internally to legal). Can you have your legal counter-propose specific language around the 60-day averaging, the 25% retro cap, and the conditional credit recoup?

Best,
Jane

Team —

I reviewed Acme's feedback. Below are recommended edits and rationales we should propose back. I attached RBI_suggested_language_floor_stabilizer.txt with the redlined clauses; copying the key points here for clarity: 

1) Averaging window: We can accept 60-day trailing average, but recommend a "rolling 60-day average measured daily" definition to preserve operational predictability. That reads: "'Floor Trigger' means when the rolling sixty (60) day average of billable units falls below the applicable committed band for two consecutive billing periods." That reduces spike risk and addresses their volatility concern.

2) Retro billing cap: We should push back on a hard 25% cap — commercial precedent exposes us to revenue leakage. Counter-proposal: permit retro-billing up to 40% of the shortfall but cap total retro charges at the lesser of (i) $150,000 or (ii) 40% of the shortfall for any single quarter. This gives us recovery while giving Acme predictability.

3) Conditional stabilizer credit: Acceptable to structure as conditional. However, tie the churn measurement to "functional production integrations" (definition to be agreed) and include an audit right for Redwood to validate. If Acme rejects seat/seat-count tracking, fall back to token-based measurement as mutually agreed.

4) Implementation: suggest adding a 30-day cure period after notification before retro billing is applied. That is: notify customer of shortfall; 30 days to cure or make-up; then retro-billing up to capped amount for the quarter.

Commercial ask: in exchange for the more permissive retro cap and the cure period, propose reducing the one-time stabilizer credit from $25K to $15K and adding a 12-month usage commit to prevent gaming. I want sign-off from Marissa on the commercial impact before we send to Jane.

Pros/Cons memo attached. LMK and I'll draft the client-facing clause.

— Laura

Jane —

Thanks for the prompt notes and for providing your redline. We reviewed internally and can accept the concept of a 60-day trailing average and a conditional stabilizer credit, with the following consolidated compromise (attached in DocuSign-ready PDF):

- Measurement: rolling 60-day average measured daily, applied to two consecutive billing periods before a floor trigger can be asserted.
- Cure window: 30 days after written notice to make up shortfall (make-up by usage or prepayment).
- Retro calculation cap: retro-billing limited to the lesser of (i) $150,000 or (ii) 40% of the shortfall for the affected quarter.
- Stabilizer credit: one-time $15,000 credit applied to first invoice, conditional on year-one net churn <= 8% (measured by functional production integrations; fallback to mutually-agreed token metric). If the condition is not met, the credit will be recouped as a one-time invoice in Q4.

Commercial trade: in exchange for the above, Redwood requests a 12-month minimum usage commitment and a mutual pledge to run a quarterly review in the first year to calibrate the banding construct.

If Acme agrees, I've attached DocuSign_Acme_OrderForm_v3.pdf with the proposed final language and a DocuSign link in related links. We're ready to route for signature as soon as you confirm.

Thanks for working through this — appreciate the pragmatism.

Best,
